scope: Later public judgments that expressly cite or discuss BP Properties Ltd v Buckler [1987] EWCA Civ 2, identified through case-name, neutral-citation and reported-citation variants.

judicial_citations.title: Colin Dawson Windows Ltd v Borough Council of King's Lynn & West Norfolk & Anor
judicial_citations.treatment: Cites and distinguishes the express-licence facts in Buckler; considers the related principle of permission during negotiations.
judicial_citations.detail: At paragraph 33 the Court of Appeal sets out the Buckler facts and quotes Dillon LJ. At paragraph 39 it distinguishes Buckler as an express-licence case while considering permission on the facts before it from the parties' negotiations. At paragraph 40 it records that the submission that Pye v Graham had implicitly overruled Buckler was withdrawn.
judicial_citations.authority_note: A later England and Wales Court of Appeal decision. Its treatment is a discussion and distinction, not a holding that Buckler was overruled.
judicial_citations.watchtower_status: Added to public/data/targets.json in this change; initial Wayback capture pending.

judicial_citations.title: Totton and Eling Town Council v Caunter & Anor
judicial_citations.court: High Court of Justice, Chancery Division
judicial_citations.treatment: Quotes and explains Buckler as a central authority on a unilateral licence affecting adverse possession.
judicial_citations.detail: The judgment identifies BP Properties v Buckler at paragraph 17, then sets out the letter, the absence of express acceptance or rejection, and Dillon LJ's reasoning in paragraphs 17–20.
judicial_citations.authority_note: A High Court decision in England and Wales; read alongside the Court of Appeal authorities and the facts of the case.
judicial_citations.watchtower_status: Added to public/data/targets.json in this change; initial Wayback capture pending.

judicial_citations.title: Smart v London Borough of Lambeth
judicial_citations.treatment: Expressly cites Buckler and applies its treatment of unilateral permission alongside the objective test for implied consent.
judicial_citations.detail: At paragraph 34 the Court of Appeal cites BP Properties v Buckler (1988) 55 P & CR 337 and explains that permission need not be contractually binding. Paragraph 35 states the requirement for an overt act or demonstrable circumstance from which permission may be inferred, judged by what a reasonable person would appreciate. Paragraph 36 discusses permission during negotiations, citing Colin Dawson Windows Ltd v King's Lynn.
judicial_citations.authority_note: A later England and Wales Court of Appeal decision. It expressly cites Buckler and explains its place in the wider permission and implied-consent authorities.
judicial_citations.watchtower_status: Added to public/data/targets.json in this change; initial Wayback capture pending.

judicial_citations.title: Smith (Personal Representative of Hugh Smith (Deceased)) and others v Molyneaux
judicial_citations.court: Judicial Committee of the Privy Council
judicial_citations.treatment: The Board expressly draws attention to Buckler and discusses unilateral permission without acceptance in the BVI statutory context.
judicial_citations.detail: At paragraph 28 the Board itself drew the parties' attention to BP Properties Ltd v Buckler, explaining that permission could be given unilaterally and did not require acceptance by the licensee. At paragraph 29 the parties accepted that the same principle applied under section 135(1) of the British Virgin Islands Registered Land Act; paragraph 30 identifies the Court of Appeal's error in requiring acknowledgment by the occupier.
judicial_citations.authority_note: A Privy Council decision arising from the British Virgin Islands. It is important comparative/persuasive material for England and Wales, not a later English Court of Appeal decision.
judicial_citations.watchtower_status: Added to public/data/targets.json in this change; initial Wayback capture pending.

verification_exclusions.title: Brown v Ridley & Anor
verification_exclusions.reason: A targeted full-text search of the published judgment returned no occurrence of “Buckler”. It is not included in the count of later decisions citing BP Properties Ltd v Buckler. A previous preliminary summary incorrectly described it as a citation; that description is corrected here.

method.notes: Do not count search snippets, duplicate mirrors or property-name matches as judicial citations unless the underlying judgment or publication has been checked. State each decision's jurisdiction and authority separately. The Watchtower static page and Wayback worker re-archive known URLs but do not automatically search all newly issued judgments; discovery of new cases requires a fresh search.
